9. Mass of 5.6 $l$ of gas at STP = $x$ g
Mass of 22.4 $l$ of gas at STP
$= \frac{x \times 22.4}{5.6} = 4x$ g
Molecular mass of the gas = $4x$
Vapour density of the gas = $\frac{4x}{2} = 2x$
Hence, the correct option is (d).

10. $n = \frac{\text{Molecular mass}}{\text{Empirical formula mass}} = 6$
Molecular formula = Empirical formula $\times 6 =$
$\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{O} \times 6 = \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O}_6$
The suitable formula for the above condition
could be $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O}_6$.
Hence, the correct option is (b).

11. Formula of trivalent metallic oxide is $\mathrm{M}_2\mathrm{O}_3$.
$31.6 \text{ g of oxygen} = 100 \text{ g of metallic oxide}$
$48 \text{ g of oxygen} = \frac{100 \times 48}{31.6}$
$= 152 \text{ g of } \mathrm{M}_2\mathrm{O}_3$
Amount of metal in $152 \text{ g of } \mathrm{M}_2\mathrm{O}_3$
$= 152 - 48 = 104 \text{ g}$
Atomic weight of metal $= \frac{104}{2} = 52$
Hence, the correct option is (c).

12. Percentage of $\text{CO}_2$ formed = 15.7 g
Amount of $\text{CO}_2$ formed for 70 g of mixture
$= \frac{15.7 \times 70}{100} = 11 \text{ g}$
$2\text{NaHCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
2 moles of $\text{NaHCO}_3 \rightarrow 1$ mole $\text{CO}_2$
44 g of $\text{CO}_2$ is obtained from $2 \times 84 \text{ g NaHCO}_3$

11 g of $\text{CO}_2$ is obtained from $\frac{2 \times 84 \times 11}{44} = 42 \text{ g}$
$\text{NaHCO}_3$
Amount of $\text{NaHCO}_3$ in the mixture = 42 g

Amount of $\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ in the mixture = 70 – 42
= 28 g
Hence, the correct option is (c).

**13.** No. of moles of $\mathrm{KClO}_3$ taken = $\frac{1225}{122.5} = 10$ moles
No. of moles of oxygen formed = $\frac{224}{22.4} = 10$
moles
$2\mathrm{KClO}_3 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{KCl} + 3\mathrm{O}_2$
10 moles of 100% pure $\mathrm{KClO}_3 \rightarrow 15$ moles of
oxygen
15 moles of oxygen = 10 moles $\mathrm{KClO}_3$
10 moles of oxygen = $\frac{100}{15}$
= 6.6 moles $\mathrm{KClO}_3$
$\therefore$ The percentage of pure $\mathrm{KClO}_3$ in the sample
= 66%
Hence, the correct option is (c).

15. Balanced chemical equation for the complete
combustion of one mole a hydrocarbon is
Given that
$\frac{y}{2} = x + 1$ [From (1)]
$y = 2x + 2$
Given that
$x + \frac{y}{4} = \frac{13}{2}$ [From (2)]
$x + \frac{2x+2}{4} = \frac{13}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{6x+2}{4} = \frac{13}{2}$
$12x = 52 - 4 = 48 \Rightarrow x = \frac{48}{12} = 4$
$\therefore \frac{y}{2} = x + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5 \Rightarrow \therefore y = 10$
$x = 4, y = 10, \mathrm{C}_x\mathrm{H}_y = \mathrm{C}_4\mathrm{H}_{10}$.
Hence, the correct option is (a).
